173	## 5. Architecture
174	
175	```
176	browser, main thread
177	  recorder: @sentry-internal/rrweb record() (DOM observation must be on the main thread)
178	    checkoutEveryNms 60 s; ring of checkout segments; keep last 10 min; cap 20 MB of event JSON
179	    privacy at record time: maskAllText, maskAllInputs, block media/editors/avatars/[data-report-block],
180	      unmask only [data-report-unmask] (level "full" only), slimDOMOptions "all", inlineImages false
181	    type-5 breadcrumbs {tag:"breadcrumb", payload} for console, clicks, fetch (URL, method, status, duration; no bodies)
182	  taint set: filled from 5 ingest points (package 2) while recording is on; lasts one page load
183	  error linking: client.on("createDsc") adds replay_id; an event processor collects error_ids, trace_ids
184	
185	  user clicks Report → buffer frozen (copy), recording continues
186	
187	web worker
188	  redaction walker: FullSnapshot text, mutation texts/adds/attributes, input events, custom payloads
189	    detectors: taint set (Aho-Corasick) → regex backstop → model (only if package 4 ships)
190	  optional: segment storage and compression, if main-thread cost is visible (package 1 measures)
191	
192	review dialog (Chakra): @sentry-internal/rrweb-player on redacted events, remaining-strings list,
193	  click-to-redact (re-runs walker), keep-last-N-minutes control, description, contact checkbox, notice
194	
195	submit (the only upload):
196	  replay_event + replay_recording envelopes, segment 0..n, ≤ 8 MiB compressed each, sequential,
197	  via client.getTransport() → /api/tunnel → Sentry
198	  then Sentry.sendFeedback({message}, {includeReplay:false}) with contexts.feedback.replay_id set
199	```

313	- Per segment:

# Bug reporter with redacted replay: implementation handoff

**For the implementing agent.** This file is self-contained: it is the whole spec, the decisions, and the test plan. Read it end to end before writing code. When this file and anything else disagree, this file wins; when this file is silent or ambiguous, stop and ask the human rather than guessing.

- Repository: `pawtograder/platform` (Next.js 15 + Supabase). Spec written against commit `329c3d8c` (Sep 27, 2026). Paths and line numbers below are from that commit; if a line has moved, search for the symbol.
- Installed SDK at that commit: `@sentry/*` and `@sentry-internal/*` 10.3.0.
- Written 2026-09-28. Status: all decisions final except the two open questions at the end.

---

## 1. Working agreement

### 1.1 Environment

- Set up the local stack by following `docs/local-dev.md` in the repo (Supabase CLI, `npx supabase db reset`, `npm run seed`, `npm run client-local` after any migration).
- The human provides these environment variables on your VM. **Never print, log, echo, or commit their values**, and never paste them into PR text, issues, or test output. Load them with `set -a; . <file the human names>; set +a`.

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `SENTRY_URL` | Base URL of the dev Sentry (self-hosted, Sentry 26.5.0) |
| `SENTRY_ORG` | `pawtograder-dev` |
| `SENTRY_PROJECT` | `pawtograder-web` (browser + Next server) |
| `SENTRY_PROJECT_EDGE` | `pawtograder-edge` (Supabase edge functions) |
| `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` | Agent token. Scopes: `org:read project:read project:releases event:read event:write`. It can read issues, events, replays, and feedback, upload source maps, and resolve issues. It cannot change settings, members, or delete data |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN` | DSN for `pawtograder-web` |
| `SENTRY_DSN_EDGE` | DSN for `pawtograder-edge` |

- Use the Sentry web API (`$SENTRY_URL/api/0/...`, header `Authorization: Bearer $SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN`) to verify what landed. You have no cluster access and must not need it.
- If a smoke event you send doesn't appear in Sentry within 60 s, stop and tell the human: that is an infrastructure fault (seen before: relay accepting events but not forwarding them), not a product bug.
- Use **synthetic data only**: the seed scripts and the canary seed (package 2a). Never point any of this at a real class.

### 1.2 Branches, PRs, done

- Base branch: `staging` (the repo default). One branch per work package, named `bug-reporter/pkg-<N>-<slug>` (e.g., `bug-reporter/pkg-0-sentry-switch`). Stack branches when a package depends on an unmerged one, and say so in the PR.
- Open a **draft PR** per package, titled `bug-reporter: pkg <N> - <summary>`. The description lists: the test IDs from section 7 that the PR makes pass, the measurements the package asks for, and anything you deferred. **Do not merge.** The human reviews and merges.
- **Done** for a package means: CI green; the package's listed test IDs pass in the tier stated; its acceptance items met; measurements recorded in the PR; no new lint warnings apart from the package 4b ratchet baseline.
- Keep everything user-visible behind the course flag (section 4.1). With the flag off, the product must behave exactly as before, except the package 0 Sentry switch and the report dialog without replay (ADR 4).

### 1.3 Never

- Add Sentry's `replayIntegration` or the feedback widget (`feedbackIntegration` with `autoInject`), or set `replaysSessionSampleRate` / `replaysOnErrorSampleRate` above 0. Section 3 explains why; test B5 enforces it.
- Upload anything replay-related before the user presses Submit.
- Unmask text, or remove a block, to make debugging easier.
- Add imports to `instrumentation-client.ts` beyond what package 0 needs. Its own comment warns that a bad import there silently takes Sentry and PostHog init down.
- Send a user's name or email to Sentry.

### 1.4 Human-owned tasks (not yours; mention in the PR if you're blocked on one)

| ID | Task | Blocks |
|---|---|---|
| HU1 | Rename the Sentry env vars in the staging deployment secrets and deploy staging | Package 0 staging acceptance |
| HU2 | Create CI secrets for the nightly and release tiers (`SENTRY_URL`, `SENTRY_ORG`, `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN`) | Package 9 |
| HU3 | Create a delete-scoped `purge-dev` token and a `SENTRY_PURGE_TOKEN` secret | Package 6b acceptance, tests H1–H3 |
| HU4 | Prod Sentry deployment (package 7) | Enabling the flag for real students |
| HU5 | Check with the Khoury privacy contact before enabling for students | Enabling the flag for real students |
| HU6 | Review and approve the generated privacy classification (package 2a output) | Merging package 2 |

---

## 2. Problem and goal

"Report a bug" in `app/course/[course_id]/UserMenu.tsx` (~line 160) links to a GitHub issue template. Reports arrive without steps, route, release, or error. `app/global-error.tsx` has a Sentry event ID but offers only the same GitHub link, and `app/error/page.tsx` says "TODO file a bug report".

**Goal:** a user who hits a problem clicks **Report a bug**, watches a redacted replay of their last few minutes, redacts anything else, adds a description, and submits. Staff open one Sentry feedback item with the replay, linked errors, breadcrumbs, release, route, and the user's role.

### Hard constraints

1. **Nothing replay-related leaves the browser until submit.** Recording lives in a rolling buffer on the device. No sampling, no auto-flush on error.
2. **Redaction runs in the browser, before review, and may be async.** The user previews exactly what will be uploaded and can redact more.
3. **Our infrastructure only.** Self-hosted Sentry. Dev: the `pawtograder-dev` org. Prod: a separate install on the app's prod infrastructure (human-owned).
4. **Text masked by default.** Only components deliberately unmasked are recorded as text.
5. **Off by default for everything.** No course or route records unless explicitly turned on (section 4).
6. **Accessible review dialog.** Passes `assertStudentPageAccessible` (`tests/e2e/axeStudentA11y.ts`). The string list is the replay's text alternative.

### Non-goals

- Always-on session replay or analytics.
- Recording canvas, images, video, or code. Monaco and the markdown editor are blocked; there is no "attach my code" option in this version.
- A per-user opt-out setting. Control is per course and per route.

---

## 3. Why the design is shaped this way

- **Backend: self-hosted Sentry replaces Bugsink.** It gives replay, feedback, and error linking. The current client (`instrumentation-client.ts`) points at a Bugsink DSN with `integrations: []`, because Bugsink supports no integrations.
- **Recorder: our own rrweb, not Sentry's `replayIntegration`.** From the installed SDK source (`@sentry-internal/replay/build/npm/esm/index.js`):
  - buffer mode forces `checkoutEveryNms: BUFFER_CHECKOUT_TIME` (60000) and clears the buffer at every checkout, so it holds 0–60 s, and no option extends it;
  - `beforeAddRecordingEvent` only sees custom events (type 5), never DOM events, and `maskFn` is synchronous;
  - the buffer is append-only compressed in a worker, so there is nothing to preview or edit;
  - opening the feedback widget, `sendFeedback` (default `includeReplay: true`), and any `replaysOnErrorSampleRate > 0` all upload the replay without asking.
- **Upload: hand-built replay envelopes through Sentry's transport.** The replay envelope format is a published stable spec (v1.3.0, develop.sentry.dev/sdk/telemetry/replays), and Sentry's mobile SDKs build it themselves. Public `@sentry/core` exports (`createEnvelope`, `createEventEnvelopeHeaders`, `prepareEvent`, `uuid4`) plus `client.getTransport().send()` are enough. The recorder is `@sentry-internal/rrweb@2.35.0`, the fork Sentry's replay player uses.
- **Redaction: schema-driven tainting, a model only if needed.** Every column, RPC result, and edge-function payload gets a privacy classification. Values from classified sources are tainted as they reach the browser, and the redaction pass removes them from recorded text. Components rendering free text or grades are blocked outright. Sentry's server-side scrubbing only matches patterns (emails, IDs), so it is a backstop.

---

## 4. Decisions (ADRs, all final)

1. **Retention: 30 days after the class ends.** A daily purge job (package 6b) deletes feedback and replays tagged with a `class_id` whose `classes.end_date` + 30 days has passed. Sentry's global `sentry.cleanup.days` (~150, human-owned) is the backstop, including for reports without a class.
2. **Who sees reports:** only platform admins and developers have Sentry access. Instructors don't get Sentry accounts. (A Pawtograder-side status view for instructors is out of scope for this handoff.)
3. **Identity:** reports and all Sentry events carry the Pawtograder user ID and role only, never name or email. This includes removing email from `Sentry.setUser` in `utils/supabase/middleware.ts` (~line 59; there is another `setUser` ~line 10). The report form has a "You may contact me about this" checkbox, sent as tag `contact_ok`. Staff look the user up by ID.
4. **Off by default:** the recorder is off unless the course flag is on and the route is listed (ADR 5). With the flag off, rrweb is not even loaded, but "Report a bug" still opens the dialog and files feedback without a replay. Where recording is on, the dialog shows a one-line notice ("This report includes a redacted recording of your last few minutes on this page").
5. **Route policy: off unless listed.** Two levels: `full` (masked text plus the unmask allowlist) and `structure` (every text node masked, no unmask). Pages that show a whole class (gradebook, submission review, rubric grading, roster, groups) are `structure` at most. Server-rendered pages that don't hydrate a `TableController` may be listed only with a taint block (section 4.3).
6. **Unmask governance:** a component unmasks text only by carrying `data-report-unmask`. CI requires CODEOWNERS review for any diff adding that attribute (grep check), and the lint rule (package 4b) plus leak test D15 check that no classified value reaches an unmasked component.
7. **Model or no model:** decided by package 4's go/no-go. Record the numbers either way.
8. **Owning the upload format:** pin `@sentry/*` and `@sentry-internal/rrweb` (and the player) to exact versions, group them in Renovate, and gate upgrades on the release-tier tests.
9. **Triage:** reports stay in Sentry. A weekly human triage promotes real bugs to GitHub issues linking to the Sentry item. Replays never go to GitHub.
10. **Schema-driven classification** as in section 3, generated by the E2E taint trace (package 2a) and approved by a human (HU6).

### 4.1 Course flag

- Add `BUG_REPORT_RECORDING: "bug-report-recording"` to `COURSE_FEATURES` in `lib/courseFeatures.ts`, and a `MANAGEABLE_COURSE_FEATURES` entry so instructors can toggle it in course settings:
  - `defaultWhenMissing: false`, `navAffectsStaff: false`
  - `title: "Bug report recordings"`
  - `description: "When on, students and staff can attach a redacted recording of their last few minutes on supported pages when they report a bug. Nothing is uploaded unless they submit a report."`
  - `switchLabel` / `ariaLabel` in the style of the existing entries.
- Turning the flag off takes effect on the next navigation or page load: the recorder stops and discards its buffer (test A6). Live realtime propagation is not required.

### 4.2 Route policy file

`lib/bugReport/routePolicy.ts`:

```ts
export type RecordingLevel = "full" | "structure";
export type RoutePolicyEntry = {
  /** Next.js app-router pattern, e.g. "/course/[course_id]/assignments/[assignment_id]" */
  pattern: string;
  level: RecordingLevel;
  /** Required true for server-rendered pages that don't hydrate a TableController */
  ssrTaint?: boolean;
};
export const ROUTE_POLICY: readonly RoutePolicyEntry[] = [ /* start with a few student pages */ ];
export function recordingLevelFor(pathname: string): RecordingLevel | null; // null = don't record
```

- Matching: `[param]` matches one segment, `[...param]` matches the rest; the most specific pattern wins.
- Test override: when `process.env.E2E_ENABLE` is set, `recordingLevelFor` also honors a JSON policy in `localStorage["bugReport.testRoutePolicy"]`. Never in production builds.
- A unit test fails if any entry whose page is a server component without a controller lacks `ssrTaint: true`, and if any `ssrTaint: true` page doesn't render the taint block.

### 4.3 Privacy classification and taint block

`lib/bugReport/privacy.ts`:

```ts
export type PiiKind = "name" | "email" | "handle" | "grade" | "free_text" | "none";
/** Every column of every table and view in public schema, key "table.column". */
export const COLUMNS: Record<string, PiiKind>;
/** RPCs: a kind for scalar/SETOF returns, or JSONPath → kind for custom/Json returns. */
export const RPCS: Record<string, PiiKind | Record<string, PiiKind>>;   // e.g. "$[*].students[*].name": "name"
/** Edge functions by wrapper name in lib/edgeFunctions.ts, JSONPath → kind. */
export const EDGE_FUNCTIONS: Record<string, Record<string, PiiKind>>;
```

- JSONPath subset: `$`, `.key`, `[*]`. Nothing else.
- SETOF RPCs returning table rows map to that table's `COLUMNS`.
- `none` must be explicit; there is no default.

Taint block, for server-rendered pages listed with `ssrTaint: true`. The server component renders `<ReportTaint values={...} />` only when the flag is on and the route is listed. It outputs:

```html
<script type="application/json" id="report-taint">{"v":1,"values":{"name":["..."],"email":["..."],"handle":["..."]}}</script>
```

The recorder reads it once at start and adds the values to the taint set.

### 4.4 Tunnel

- `app/api/tunnel/route.ts` must read the body as bytes: `arrayBuffer()`, split at the first `\n` to read the envelope header.
- It forwards only to the host and project ID parsed from `NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN`, returning 403 for anything else. This replaces `NEXT_PUBLIC_BUGSINK_HOST`.
- Edge functions send server-to-server with `SENTRY_DSN_EDGE` and never use the tunnel.

---

## 5. Architecture

```
browser, main thread
  recorder: @sentry-internal/rrweb record() (DOM observation must be on the main thread)
    checkoutEveryNms 60 s; ring of checkout segments; keep last 10 min; cap 20 MB of event JSON
    privacy at record time: maskAllText, maskAllInputs, block media/editors/avatars/[data-report-block],
      unmask only [data-report-unmask] (level "full" only), slimDOMOptions "all", inlineImages false
    type-5 breadcrumbs {tag:"breadcrumb", payload} for console, clicks, fetch (URL, method, status, duration; no bodies)
  taint set: filled from 5 ingest points (package 2) while recording is on; lasts one page load
  error linking: client.on("createDsc") adds replay_id; an event processor collects error_ids, trace_ids

  user clicks Report → buffer frozen (copy), recording continues

web worker
  redaction walker: FullSnapshot text, mutation texts/adds/attributes, input events, custom payloads
    detectors: taint set (Aho-Corasick) → regex backstop → model (only if package 4 ships)
  optional: segment storage and compression, if main-thread cost is visible (package 1 measures)

review dialog (Chakra): @sentry-internal/rrweb-player on redacted events, remaining-strings list,
  click-to-redact (re-runs walker), keep-last-N-minutes control, description, contact checkbox, notice

submit (the only upload):
  replay_event + replay_recording envelopes, segment 0..n, ≤ 8 MiB compressed each, sequential,
  via client.getTransport() → /api/tunnel → Sentry
  then Sentry.sendFeedback({message}, {includeReplay:false}) with contexts.feedback.replay_id set
```

---

## 6. Work packages

Order: **0 → 1 → {2, 2a-phase1, 3, 4b} → 2a-phase2 → 4 (only if needed) → 5 → 6 → 6b → 9.** Package 7 and 8 are human-owned or optional.

### Package 0: switch from Bugsink to Sentry
- **Tunnel:** rewrite per section 4.4.
- **`next.config.ts`:**
  - replace `usingBugsink = !!process.env.SENTRY_URL` (~line 20) with `const usingBugsink = process.env.SENTRY_IS_BUGSINK === "1"`, so release create, finalize, and deploy work on real Sentry;
  - set `tunnelRoute: false` (~line 203); `tunnel: "/api/tunnel"` in the client config already routes events;
  - update `hasSentryDsn` (~line 200) and any Bugsink wording in the source-map upload guard (~line 272) to the new variable names.
- **Env var renames:**
  - `NEXT_PUBLIC_BUGSINK_DSN` → `NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN` in `instrumentation-client.ts` (~line 36), `sentry.server.config.ts`, `sentry.edge.config.ts`, and the `Dockerfile` ARGs.
  - Edge functions keep their own `SENTRY_DSN` (`supabase/functions/_shared/SentryInit.ts`); set it to the edge DSN.
  - Keep reading the old names as a fallback for one release, with a console warning.
- **ADR 3 identity change:** remove `email` from `Sentry.setUser` calls; set tag `role` where the role is known.
- Keep `integrations: []` and both replay sample rates at 0.
- **Tests:** F3, F4, G1, B5 (PR tier).
- **Accept:**
  - locally, an error from the app lands in `pawtograder-web` (check via API) with a resolved stack trace after a source-map upload;
  - F3 passes, and fails against the old tunnel;
  - staging acceptance waits on HU1.

### Package 1: recorder and ring buffer
- Add exact-pinned dependencies `@sentry-internal/rrweb@2.35.0` and the matching `@sentry-internal/rrweb-player`.
- `lib/bugReport/recorder.ts`, started from a client component mounted in the root layout next to `<StaleBundleRecovery />`. It is dynamically imported only when the course flag is on and `recordingLevelFor(pathname)` is non-null.
- Record per section 5. The ring buffer drops whole oldest segments to stay within 10 minutes and 20 MB, so the kept window always starts with Meta + FullSnapshot.
- Level `structure`: mask every text node, ignoring `data-report-unmask`.
- Measure buffer size at 5 and 10 minutes, and main-thread long tasks, on the gradebook (200 students) and the rubric grading page. If recorder long tasks exceed 5% of main-thread time, move segment storage and compression to a worker.
- **Tests:** A1, A2, A4, A6, B1–B4, C1–C6 (PR tier); K1, K2 (nightly).

### Package 2: classification, ingest, taint set
- Create `lib/bugReport/privacy.ts` (section 4.3).
- **Initial draft:** a script generates it from two sources, and the human reviews it (HU6):
  - column-name heuristics (`name`, `sortable_name`, `email`, `*_username`, `score*`, `body`, `message`, and so on);
  - `docs/operations/data-retention.md` §"PII / grades".
- **Exhaustiveness:** extend `scripts/PostprocessSupabaseTypes.ts` (run by `npm run client` / `client-local`) to fail when any column, view field, RPC, or edge-function wrapper lacks an entry.
- **Five ingest points** (all behind "recording is on"):
  1. A global `window.fetch` wrapper, installed before any Supabase client is constructed, because supabase-js captures `fetch` at construction. It covers PostgREST, RPC (`/rest/v1/rpc/<fn>`), edge functions, `/api/*`, and the second browser client in `components/github/link-account.tsx` (~line 61).
  2. `TableController` ingest: `initialData` (constructor ~line 1824), `_addRow`, `_updateRow`. This carries the server-hydrated roster from `lib/ssrUtils.ts` through `hooks/useCourseController.tsx`.
  3. Realtime: `RealtimeChannelManager` broadcast handling (`_routeMessage`, ~line 521) and `postgres_changes` (~line 944), plus `hooks/useMeetingWindows.tsx` (~line 144). The broadcast envelope has `table` and full rows for most tables; ID-only broadcasts refetch through the fetch wrapper.
  4. The taint block (section 4.3).
  5. The auth session (`auth.getSession()`): the user's own email and `user_metadata`.
- **Select parser (~150 lines):**
  - maps PostgREST response keys to `table.column` using the URL's `select=`;
  - resolves an alias if present, otherwise the relation name;
  - resolves FK hints (`!fk`) through `Relationships` in `utils/supabase/SupabaseTypes.d.ts`;
  - spreads and casts don't occur and need no support.
- **Matching:**
  - At ingest, expand `name` values into variants: first and last tokens, "Last, First", lower case, and the `name (real_name)` form from `components/ui/person-name.tsx`.
  - Match strings of 3+ characters, case- and whitespace-normalized, with Aho-Corasick.
  - Never string-match grades, initials, or strings under 3 characters; those are blocked structurally (package 3).
- Regex backstop: emails, 9-digit NUIDs, `mailto:`.
- **Tests:** unit tests for select resolution (aliases, hints, embeds); D1, D2, D4–D7, D16 (PR tier).

### Package 2a: dynamic taint trace in E2E
Builds and checks the classification by observing where PII actually flows.
- **Phase 1** (needs only the seed and the select parser):
  - **Canary seed:** a `canary` option for `createClass` and `createUsersInClass` in `tests/e2e/TestingUtils.ts` and for `scripts/SeedDemoClass.ts`. Extend the existing functions with an optional parameter; don't fork them. Every PII field gets a unique canary that passes validation:
    - names: unique first and last tokens;
    - emails and handles: valid formats with a unique local part;
    - free text: sentences containing a token;
    - grades: distinctive values such as 87.31.
    Write a registry `value → {kind, table.column, rowId}`.
  - **Source discovery:** a Playwright fixture scans for canaries in HTTP responses (`page.on("response")`), websocket frames (`page.on("websocket")` → `framereceived`), the initial HTML, and `self.__next_f`. For each hit it records the source, key or JSONPath, and kind.
  - **Sink discovery:** after each step, scan DOM text and attributes for canaries and variants. Record the route, selector, and `data-sentry-component`, which needs the full build profile: `SENTRY_BUILD_PROFILE=ci-fast` disables component annotation.
  - **Outputs** (committed, human-reviewed):
    - `lib/bugReport/generated/privacy.observed.json`: `[{source, key, kind, firstSeenIn}]`
    - `lib/bugReport/generated/pii-sinks.json`: `{route: {component: kinds[]}}`
  - **CI fails when:**
    - an observed flow lacks a classification;
    - a classified value is rendered by a component carrying `data-report-unmask`.
    Canaries never observed are reported as coverage gaps.
- **Phase 2** (after packages 1 and 3): run the recorder and redaction in the trace job and assert no canary in any would-be upload for every E2E test.
- **Tests:** I1–I4 (nightly).

### Package 3: redaction walker and structural blocking
- A worker that walks the frozen events: FullSnapshot text nodes, mutation `texts`, `adds`, and `attributes` (`title`, `alt`, `aria-label`, `placeholder`, `href`), input events (incremental source 5), and custom-event payloads.
- Rebuild text per block element with offsets, so a name split across nodes (`<b>Jane</b> Doe`) matches, then map spans back to node IDs. Keep a node-id → text map replayed forward through mutations.
- Detector interface `(text: string) => Promise<Span[]>`: taint set, then the regex backstop, then the model if package 4 ships.
- **`<ReportBlock>`:** a wrapper component that sets `data-report-block`. rrweb records it as a sized placeholder, and review can't unblock it. Apply it to:
  - avatars and initials;
  - every component that renders `free_text` or `grade` values, per `pii-sinks.json` once it exists (seed by hand from `PersonName`, help-request, discussion, and gradebook cell components).
- **Tests:** D3, D8–D15, D17 (PR tier).

### Package 4: model detector (conditional)
- Build only if the leak tests, with taint set and blocking alone, still leak free text that isn't blocked. Otherwise record the numbers in the PR and skip.
- If built:
  - GLiNER-PII-small ONNX UINT8 (~200 MB) via GLiNER.js, WebGPU with WASM fallback, in the package 3 worker.
  - Lazy-loaded on the first report and cached in IndexedDB. Weights are served from our origin, and `utils/csp.ts` already allows `wasm-unsafe-eval` and `worker-src blob:`.
  - Runs only over text that survived masking.
- **Go** if detection takes ≤ 5 s on 50 KB of text on a mid-range laptop.
- **Tests:** J1–J3.

### Package 4b: type-level guardrail
- Extend `scripts/PostprocessSupabaseTypes.ts` to brand classified `Row` columns as `Pii<kind, T>`. Leave `Insert` and `Update` unbranded.
- A typescript-eslint rule that flags two things:
  - rendering a `Pii` value inside an element with `data-report-unmask`;
  - rendering `free_text` or `grade` values outside `<ReportBlock>`.
- Warn mode. Record the violation count in the PR as the baseline; CI fails only if the count rises.

### Package 5: review dialog and entry points
- A Chakra dialog per section 5. With recording off, show only the description and contact checkbox; submit sends feedback without a replay.
- Entry points:
  - UserMenu "Report a bug";
  - a "Report this" action on `toaster.error` toasts (`components/ui/toaster.tsx` already renders `toast.action`), with the error event ID prefilled;
  - `app/global-error.tsx`, which renders its own `<html>` without Chakra, so it needs a minimal plain-HTML form.
- Cancel sends nothing.
- **Tests:** A1 (dialog without replay), E1–E10 (PR tier).

### Package 6: envelope builder and submit
- Per segment:
  - `prepareEvent` a `replay_event` with `replay_id` = `event_id` = one fresh `uuid4()`, `segment_id` 0..n, `replay_type: "buffer"`, `replay_start_timestamp` (first kept event), `timestamp`, `urls`, `error_ids`, `trace_ids`;
  - body = `{"segment_id":n}\n` + zlib-compressed JSON of the events (`CompressionStream("deflate")`);
  - `createEnvelope` with both items; send sequentially via `client.getTransport().send()`.

- **Retries:** exponential backoff for 5xx and network errors, up to 3 tries per segment. A 429 aborts and shows "try again later".

- Tags on the feedback and every replay event: `class_id`, `role`, `route` (pattern, not concrete path), `release`, `contact_ok`.
- **Tests:** F1, F2, F5, F6 (PR tier); F7, F8 (nightly and release tiers, pending HU2).

### Package 6b: retention purge job
- A Supabase edge function `bug-report-retention-purge`, scheduled daily with `pg_cron`; see existing `cron.schedule` usage in `supabase/migrations/` for the pattern.
- For each class with `classes.end_date + 30 days < now()`, it deletes Sentry feedback and replays tagged with that `class_id` via the Sentry API, using `SENTRY_PURGE_TOKEN` (HU3).
- Each run logs counts only, no IDs or content.
- The first step is to confirm that the Sentry 26.5 API endpoints for deleting replays and feedback exist. If they don't, stop and report.
- **Tests:** H1–H3 (nightly, pending HU3).

### Package 9: CI tiers
- **PR tier:** add the bug-reporter specs to the existing E2E jobs (see `.github/workflows/lint.yml`), with the fake tunnel fixture.
- **Nightly workflow:** `bug-reporter-nightly.yml`. Scheduled, plus PRs labeled `bug-reporter-full`. Full build profile, with the real dev Sentry through the secrets from HU2. Runs F7, F8, H, I, K.
- **Release workflow:** runs the release-tier tests on `@sentry/*` or rrweb version bumps (Renovate group) and before promoting staging to main.

Package 7 (prod Sentry) is human-owned (HU4). Package 8 (offline labeling and fine-tune of the model with Claude-labeled data) happens only if package 4 is built and underperforms; not part of this handoff.

# Sentry research report (dev Sentry 26.5.0)

Scripts in this directory; run after `set -a; . ~/.config/sentry-dev/pawtograder.env; set +a`.

## Verdicts
- Open Q2 (buffer replay ingest): relay returns 200 for every replay envelope, but NO replay of any kind is stored (even real @sentry/browser 10.3.0 session replays). Infrastructure fault, reported to the human. The recording-segments endpoint 500s for every id, which suggests replay blob storage is misconfigured. Blocks F7 only.
- Open Q1 (size): 8.0 MiB → 200, 9.9 MiB → 200, 10.5 MiB → 413 "envelope exceeded size limits for type 'replay_recording'". The limit is 10 MiB per item, including the segment_id line. Treat 413 as permanent (no retry). The 8 MiB cap is OK.
- 6b precondition: GO. The endpoints exist (403 to the agent token). The purge token needs project:write (replays) and event:admin (feedback).
- Feedback works: a feedback issue with tags class_id/role/route/release/contact_ok; contexts.feedback.replay_id is set and Sentry adds contexts.replay.replay_id.
- Linked error: contexts.replay.replay_id + tags.replayId; Discover `replayId:<id>` finds it.

## Shapes that got 2xx
- Endpoint: getEnvelopeEndpointWithUrlEncodedAuth(dsnFromString(dsn)) via @sentry/core createTransport.
- Segment: replay_event item + replay_recording item (same as the SDK's createReplayEnvelope). The event has event_id=replay_id, segment_id, replay_type, replay_start_timestamp, timestamp, urls, error_ids, trace_ids, tags, user:{id}, platform:"javascript". The recording body is `{"segment_id":n}\n` + zlib deflate(JSON events).
- Feedback item {"type":"feedback"} with contexts.feedback {message, url, source:"api", replay_id, associated_event_id}.

## API (base /api/0)
- Replay details: GET /organizations/{org}/replays/{id}/ (tags, error_ids, trace_ids, count_segments, count_errors, user, urls, replay_type)
- Recording: GET /projects/{org}/{proj}/replays/{id}/recording-segments/?per_page=100 (inflated JSON [[seg0],...]); one segment: …/recording-segments/{n}/?download
- Replays by tag: GET /organizations/{org}/replays/?project=-1&statsPeriod=90d&query=class_id:N
- Feedback by tag: GET /organizations/{org}/issues/?project=-1&statsPeriod=90d&query=issue.category:feedback class_id:N
- Discover linked errors: GET /organizations/{org}/events/?dataset=discover&field=id&query=replayId:<id>
- Delete a replay: DELETE /projects/{org}/{proj}/replays/{id}/ (project:write, async, 204 even with no data)
- Bulk replay delete: POST /projects/{org}/{proj}/replays/jobs/delete/ {"data":{"rangeStart","rangeEnd","environments":[],"query":"class_id:N"}} → 201; poll GET …/jobs/delete/{job_id}/
- Delete feedback issues: DELETE /organizations/{org}/issues/?id=…&id=… → 204 (event:admin, ≤1000 per call). With ids given, the query is ignored. List ids by tag first, then delete by id.
- Delete one issue: DELETE /organizations/{org}/issues/{id}/ → 202 (5 per 5 s)

## SDK gotchas (@sentry/core 10.3.0)
- serializeEnvelope appends Uint8Array payloads unchanged (binary safe).
- transport.send() quietly drops items that are rate-limited from an earlier 429 and returns {} with no statusCode. Treat a missing status as failure.
- The browser transport sets keepalive for bodies ≤ 60 KB. That's fine at submit, but B3 must only assert no keepalive BEFORE submit.
- sendFeedback: includeReplay is only read by replayIntegration (not installed). It calls getCurrentScope().setTags(tags), which leaks tags to later errors, so call it inside withScope or set the tags in the hook. It defaults url to location.href (concrete path), so pass url explicitly (D17).
- beforeSendFeedback is a client hook (client.on), sync, and mutates in place; it can't drop the event. beforeSend does NOT run for feedback.
- Sentry infers user.ip_address (private ingress IP) even when none is sent. Open question to the human: send ip_address null, or turn on the org's "Prevent storing IP addresses".

-- alerts, so a row aged off invitation_date would be refreshed a few milliseconds before being
     -- asked how old it is — the "still stuck" alert could never fire at all. A dated class is aged
     -- from start_date; an undated one (which the sweep will not touch, and which this function
     -- reports so somebody fills the dates in) is aged from when the class was created.
     and (
           case when c.start_date is not null
                then c.start_date <= current_date - p_days
                else c.created_at < now() - make_interval(days => p_days)
           end
         )
     -- Don't keep alerting about classes that are long over.
     and (c.end_date is null or c.end_date >= current_date - 30)
     -- Nor about ancient course shells that were never configured and never will be.
     and c.created_at > now() - interval '365 days'
     -- This enrollment's OWN invitation must be nearly expired. The sweep rewrites invitation_date
     -- every staleness period, so a row's invitation age cycles between zero and that threshold and
     -- can never reach the p_days figure the class bound uses; requiring p_days here would mean the
     -- alert never fires at all. Requiring a couple of days instead fires far too eagerly in the
     -- other direction — a student who joins a term-old class is swept within the hour and would be
     -- reported as stuck two days later, while their invitation was still valid for five more.
     --
     -- Just under the sweep threshold is the setting that means something: the invitation has been
     -- outstanding almost its entire life and has still not been accepted. It holds for the day or
     -- so before the next re-invite, which at hourly cadence is ample.
     --
     -- Falls back to updated_at for a role with no invitation at all. user_roles has no created_at,
     -- and set_updated_at_on_user_roles makes updated_at "last modified" rather than "created", so
     -- this is a lower bound on the row's age: it can delay an alert for a recently edited role,
     -- which is the safe direction.
     and coalesce(ur.invitation_date, ur.updated_at) < now() - make_interval(days => p_invitation_age_days)
   group by c.id, c.slug, c.github_org, c.start_date, c.end_date, c.archived
$$;

revoke all on function public.get_stuck_org_membership_alerts(int, int) from public;
grant execute on function public.get_stuck_org_membership_alerts(int, int) to service_role;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Cron: invoke the membership reconciler hourly.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Hourly rather than the repo reconciler's 15 minutes: the staleness threshold is measured in days,
-- so a faster cadence would buy nothing and only spend GitHub API budget. Offset off the hour to
-- avoid landing on top of the other :00 jobs.
create or replace function public.invoke_github_membership_reconciler_background_task()
returns void
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = public
as $$
begin
  perform public.call_edge_function_internal(
    '/functions/v1/github-membership-reconciler',
    'POST',
    '{"Content-type":"application/json","x-supabase-webhook-source":"github-membership-reconciler"}'::jsonb,
    '{}'::jsonb,
    5000,
    null, null, null, null, null
  );
end;
$$;

revoke all on function public.invoke_github_membership_reconciler_background_task() from public;
grant execute on function public.invoke_github_membership_reconciler_background_task() to service_role;

    if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
    runs-on: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.trusted == 'true' && 'pawtograder-ci' || 'ubuntu-latest' }}
    steps:
      # First, before any checkout: an untrusted ref must not reach the code.
      - name: Require a trusted ref
        if: ${{ needs.gate.result != 'success' || needs.gate.outputs.trusted != 'true' }}
        run: |
          echo "::error title=Untrusted ref::This check cannot run for this PR. ${{ needs.gate.result != 'success' && 'The trust gate could not resolve a verdict — see the gate job.' || 'Add the contributor to the pawtograder-contributors team, or have a ci-approval reviewer approve the run (Review deployments on the PR).' }}"
          exit 1
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          # MERGE ref; see the `lint` job's checkout for why.
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number && format('refs/pull/{0}/merge', github.event.pull_request.number) || github.sha }}
          # Fork code under pull_request_target is admitted by the trust gate
          # (_trust-gate.yml: write access or a ci-approval reviewer), which every
          # job doing this depends on. actions/checkout refuses it without this flag.
          allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true
          persist-credentials: false
      # refs/pull/N/merge is MUTABLE: GitHub recomputes it in the background
      # after every push, so resolving it at checkout time is not the same as
      # resolving the head SHA the gate vetted. Two ways that bites — a stale
      # ref right after `synchronize`, where the required contexts would go
      # green on a head nobody tested; and a ref that moved between the gate
      # and here, which would run a commit whose pusher was never checked, on
      # the self-hosted pool. That is exactly the check-then-use window
      # _trust-gate.yml claims not to have, so close it here rather than
      # weaken the claim.

      # `git cat-file` rather than HEAD^2: the checkout is shallow, so the
      # parent objects are absent even though the commit records their hashes.
      - name: Verify the merge ref contains the vetted head
        if: github.event.pull_request.number
        env:
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          merged_head=$(git cat-file -p HEAD | awk '/^parent /{print $2}' | sed -n 2p)

            echo "::error title=Merge ref does not match the vetted head::This checkout contains ${merged_head}, but the trust gate approved ${HEAD_SHA}. The merge ref moved or is stale; re-run this job." >&2

---

## Error reporting (Sentry / self-hosted Bugsink)

Pawtograder reports errors through the Sentry SDK, but the client is configured
for a **Sentry-compatible** backend and the web app is wired specifically for
[**Bugsink**](https://www.bugsink.com/) — a lightweight, single-container,
self-hostable error tracker. If you have only minimal resources, **self-hosting
Bugsink is the recommended option** (it speaks the Sentry DSN protocol, so the
same SDK config works against either).

Two surfaces, two variables:

- **Web app (build-time).** `NEXT_PUBLIC_BUGSINK_DSN` (and
  `NEXT_PUBLIC_BUGSINK_HOST`) are `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` vars, so they are **baked into
  the web image at build time** — pass them as `docker build --build-arg`s, not
  runtime env. When the DSN is unset the Sentry webpack integration is skipped
  entirely (fine for local dev). The client posts through a `/api/tunnel` route
  and runs with no Sentry integrations (Bugsink doesn't support them).
- **Edge Functions (runtime).** `SENTRY_DSN` (and optional `SENTRY_DEBUG`) are
  read at runtime from the `sentry` bundle:

  ```sh
  scripts/setup-openbao-edge-functions.sh \
    --env production --bundle sentry \
    --from-file .secrets/sentry-production.env
  ```

`SENTRY_RELEASE` / `SENTRY_ENVIRONMENT` are optional on both surfaces for tagging
releases and environments. Leave everything unset to disable error reporting.

---

## Other integrations

These are configured the same way — a bundle of env vars provisioned into the web
and/or edge-functions Secret. See
[`scripts/setup-openbao-edge-functions.sh --list`](./scripts/setup-openbao-edge-functions.sh)
for the full set and the [chart README](./charts/pawtograder/README.md) for how
they're mounted:

- **AWS Chime** (office-hours video) — `aws-chime` bundle.
- **Canvas / SIS** roster sync — `canvas` / `sis` bundles.
- **LLM / MCP** hints — `mcp` bundle.
  #   MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2             bound the arena count
  #   MALLOC_MMAP_THRESHOLD_=131072  fixed 128Ki threshold (also disables the
  #                                  dynamic one), so eszip copies are mmapped
  #                                  and returned to the OS on free
  extraEnv:
    - name: MALLOC_ARENA_MAX
      value: "2"
    - name: MALLOC_MMAP_THRESHOLD_

  envFromSecrets:
    - pawtograder-github-app
    - pawtograder-discord
    - pawtograder-canvas
    - pawtograder-llm
    - pawtograder-e2e
    # Edge functions read SENTRY_DSN for server-side error reporting
    # (_shared/HandlerUtils.ts). The secret also carries the frontend
    # NEXT_PUBLIC_BUGSINK_* keys, which are inert in the Deno runtime.
    - pawtograder-sentry

    # environment, which is why notification email never sent: the processor read "no SMTP host"

    # those names as well as the older SMTP_PASSWORD / SMTP_FROM.
    - pawtograder-smtp
  email:
    # Explicit, so missing SMTP config is a reported failure rather than a silent deferral.
    enabled: "true"
  e2e:
    enabled: true
    mockGitHub: true

- Export `NEXT_PUBLIC_PAWTOGRADER_WEB_URL` to match the prod server port **before** building — `npm run build` bakes the value into the bundle, and changing the env at runtime will not update an existing `.next` output. Re-export and rebuild from a clean `.next` directory whenever you switch modes: `export NEXT_PUBLIC_PAWTOGRADER_WEB_URL=http://localhost:3001 && rm -rf .next && npm run build`
  - Start only the prod server: `PORT=3001 npm run start`
  - Run Playwright with matching **`BASE_URL`**: `BASE_URL=http://localhost:3001 npx playwright test ...` (the **built** app URL comes from the build step above; Playwright only needs `BASE_URL` to match where `next start` listens).
- **E2E — dev-mode (only for rapid iteration on a single test)**: With local Supabase running and `npm run dev` (port 3000), run **`npm run test:e2e:local`** — it sets `BASE_URL=http://localhost:3000` to match the dev server (`playwright.config.ts`). Ensure **`SUPABASE_URL`**, **`SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`**, and **`SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`** are in `.env.local` or exported: `tests/e2e/TestingUtils.ts` loads `.env.local` via dotenv and uses those values (plus the service role for the admin client) for setup and auth helpers. Do not use this mode for running the whole suite.
- **GitHub App credentials are not required locally** — E2E tests set `E2E_ENABLE=true` and use the Edge Functions' E2E bypass instead of making real GitHub calls. Dummy `GITHUB_APP_ID=1` / `GITHUB_PRIVATE_KEY_STRING` values are enough; the Edge Function runtime just needs _some_ RSA key to initialize its GitHub App client at module load. If you see `Circuit breaker active` errors, something is wrong with the E2E bypass (or you're hitting the real GitHub path), not a missing-credentials issue. To clear a tripped breaker after fixing the root cause: `docker exec -i supabase_db_pawtograder-platform psql -U postgres -d postgres -c "UPDATE public.github_circuit_breakers SET state='closed', open_until=now() WHERE state='open';"`.
- **E2E prerequisites — Edge Functions and secrets**: Several E2E tests invoke Supabase Edge Functions (e.g. `autograder-create-submission`, `autograder-submit-feedback`). For these to work locally:
  1. **Serve Edge Functions**: `npx supabase functions serve --env-file .env.local`
  2. **`.env.local` must contain** (in addition to Supabase keys):
     - `E2E_ENABLE=true` — enables the E2E testing bypass in Edge Functions
     - `END_TO_END_SECRET=not-a-secret` — shared secret between the test runner and Edge Functions
     - `REDACTED` — must match the value stored in the Supabase DB vault (`vault.secrets` table, name `edge-function-secret`). The local Supabase seed sets this to `some-secret-value`.
     - `GITHUB_APP_ID=1` and `GITHUB_PRIVATE_KEY_STRING` (any valid RSA private key) — required for the Edge Function runtime to boot (the GitHub App client initializes at module load). E2E tests bypass GitHub auth, so dummy values work.
  3. **No need to run `npm run seed`** before E2E tests — tests create their own fixtures. Seeding is only needed for manual browser testing.
  4. You can verify Edge Functions are working: `curl http://127.0.0.1:54321/functions/v1/autograder-create-submission` should return `{"error":{"recoverable":false,"message":"No token provided","details":"No token provided"}}` (not `WORKER_ERROR`).
- **Build**: `npm run build` (requires ~8 GB memory via `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8000`).
- **Format**: `npm run format` (Prettier auto-fix).

### Operator CLI

`npm run cli -- <command>` (entry `cli/index.ts`) drives course operations through the `cli` Edge Function. Every command POSTs `{ command, params }` to that one function, which dispatches through the registry in `supabase/functions/cli/router.ts`.

The same source ships to npm as [`@pawtograder/cli`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@pawtograder/cli), so instructors can run `npx @pawtograder/cli <command>` without a checkout. See [`packages/cli/`](./packages/cli/) for the packaging and release process; `npm run cli:build` builds and smoke-tests the published bundle locally.

Requires **`pawtograder login`** with an API token from Settings → API Tokens: `cli:read` for the read commands, `cli:write` for the ones that mutate. Point `--url` at the deployment's **API gateway origin** (`https://api.<hostname>`), not the web host — the web host serves the app, not the function.

     - `END_TO_END_SECRET=not-a-secret` — shared secret between the test runner and Edge Functions
     - `REDACTED` — must match the value stored in the Supabase DB vault (`vault.secrets` table, name `edge-function-secret`). The local Supabase seed sets this to `some-secret-value`.
     - `GITHUB_APP_ID=1` and `GITHUB_PRIVATE_KEY_STRING` (any valid RSA private key) — required for the Edge Function runtime to boot (the GitHub App client initializes at module load). E2E tests bypass GitHub auth, so dummy values work.
  3. **No need to run `npm run seed`** before E2E tests — tests create their own fixtures. Seeding is only needed for manual browser testing.
  4. You can verify Edge Functions are working: `curl http://127.0.0.1:54321/functions/v1/autograder-create-submission` should return `{"error":{"recoverable":false,"message":"No token provided","details":"No token provided"}}` (not `WORKER_ERROR`).
- **Build**: `npm run build` (requires ~8 GB memory via `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8000`).
- **Format**: `npm run format` (Prettier auto-fix).

### Operator CLI

`npm run cli -- <command>` (entry `cli/index.ts`) drives course operations through the `cli` Edge Function. Every command POSTs `{ command, params }` to that one function, which dispatches through the registry in `supabase/functions/cli/router.ts`.

The same source ships to npm as [`@pawtograder/cli`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@pawtograder/cli), so instructors can run `npx @pawtograder/cli <command>` without a checkout. See [`packages/cli/`](./packages/cli/) for the packaging and release process; `npm run cli:build` builds and smoke-tests the published bundle locally.

Requires **`pawtograder login`** with an API token from Settings → API Tokens: `cli:read` for the read commands, `cli:write` for the ones that mutate. Point `--url` at the deployment's **API gateway origin** (`https://api.<hostname>`), not the web host — the web host serves the app, not the function.

-- Self-healing for GitHub ORG MEMBERSHIP, the half of the GitHub integration that had none.
--
-- What was missing. Every automated path that invites a user to a class's GitHub org is gated on
-- `user_roles.invitation_date IS NULL` (github-async-worker sync_student_team / sync_staff_team,
-- and the autograder-sync-student-team backstop), and github-repo-webhook stamps that column the
-- moment GitHub reports `member_invited`. A GitHub org invitation expires after 7 days, and GitHub
-- emits no event when it does. So one unaccepted invitation put the enrollment into a state that no
-- automation could ever leave:
--
--     github_org_confirmed = false  +  invitation_date IS NOT NULL  +  no org membership
--
-- and because everything downstream keys off `github_org_confirmed` (the team-sync member lists
-- filter on it, `sync_repo_permissions_for_student` fires on the false->true transition), that
-- student silently had no team membership and no repo access for the rest of the term. The only
-- repairs in production were a student logging in (app/auth/callback re-runs github-user-sync) or
-- pressing "Sync GitHub Account" — which is exactly what the steady stream of "Fix GitHub button
-- made changes" Sentry events was recording. github-repo-reconciler covers repositories only;
-- discord-reconciler covers Discord membership; nothing covered this.
--
-- This migration adds the missing reconciler:

-- Package 6b: retention purge (ADR 1)
-- ===========================================================================

-- it already swept today, puts never-swept classes first, and keeps what was deleted countable
-- without logging ids. It is internal state for the service role: RLS on with no policies, and no
-- grants to anon or authenticated.

  class_id bigint primary key references public.classes (id) on delete cascade,
  first_purged_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  last_purged_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  last_feedback_deleted integer not null default 0,
  last_replays_deleted integer not null default 0,
  total_feedback_deleted bigint not null default 0,
  total_replays_deleted bigint not null default 0
);

alter table public.bug_report_retention_purges enable row level security;
revoke all on table public.bug_report_retention_purges from public, anon, authenticated;
grant select, insert, update, delete on table public.bug_report_retention_purges to service_role;

comment on table public.bug_report_retention_purges is
  'Last Sentry retention sweep per class (bug-report-retention-purge). Service role only.';

-- checks the same rule again before deleting anything). Classes with no end_date are never due.

-- Sentry over the same lookback, which must be at least sentry.cleanup.days; past it, everything a
-- class could have is already gone. Until then a class is swept daily, because a report can still be
-- filed against an archived course after its first purge.
--
-- Not swept in the last p_resweep_after_hours, so a doubled or retried cron call does no extra work.
-- Never-swept classes first, then the longest-ago sweep, so a run cut short by its limit rotates.
create or replace function public.get_bug_report_retention_purge_candidates(
  p_grace_days integer,
  p_lookback_days integer,
  p_resweep_after_hours integer,
  p_limit integer
) returns table (class_id bigint, end_date date)
language sql
stable
security definer

as $$
  select c.id, c.end_date
    from public.classes c
    left join public.bug_report_retention_purges p on p.class_id = c.id

     and (c.end_date::timestamp at time zone 'UTC') + make_interval(days => p_grace_days) < now()
     and (c.end_date::timestamp at time zone 'UTC') + make_interval(days => p_grace_days + p_lookback_days) > now()
     and (p.last_purged_at is null or p.last_purged_at < now() - make_interval(hours => p_resweep_after_hours))

   limit greatest(p_limit, 0)
$$;

volatile

  )

  );

$$;

grant execute on function public.invoke_bug_report_retention_purge_background_task() to service_role;

-- Daily, off the hour so it doesn't land on the other :00 jobs.
do $cron$
begin
  if exists (select 1 from pg_extension where extname = 'pg_cron') then
    if exists (select 1 from cron.job where jobname = 'bug-report-retention-purge') then
      perform cron.unschedule('bug-report-retention-purge');

    );
    raise notice 'Bug report retention purge cron scheduled daily';
  end if;
exception
  when insufficient_privilege then
    raise notice 'Skipping bug-report-retention-purge cron schedule: insufficient privilege';
end;
$cron$;

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Setup, Commands, and Local Dev

See [AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md) for build/test/lint commands, local Supabase setup, seeding, ports, and known issues. Everything there applies here too.

Additional commands not in AGENTS.md:

```bash
npm run client-local          # Regenerate TS types from local Supabase schema
npm run client                # Regenerate TS types from remote staging schema
npm run typecheck:functions   # Deno type-check Edge Functions
npx jest path/to/test.ts      # Run a single Jest test
npx playwright test path.spec.ts  # Run a single Playwright test
```

## Architecture

### Supabase Client Patterns

Two typed client factories (both use generated `Database` type from `utils/supabase/SupabaseTypes.d.ts`):

- `utils/supabase/server.ts` — server-side client using Next.js cookies (Server Components, Route Handlers)
- `utils/supabase/client.ts` — browser client with Realtime worker; also exports `createAdminClient` using service role key (server-only)

# Writing rules for this project

<!-- maintainer: bump the version string below on every release; see README "Maintainer notes" -->

These rules apply to all prose in this repository. They were generated by `/ai-slop:init` from the [ai-slop-skill](https://github.com/se-uhd/ai-slop-skill) (skill version 2026-07) and combine the writing rules maintained by the [Software Engineering Group at Heidelberg University](https://github.com/se-uhd) with a general AI-trope catalog from [tropes.fyi](https://tropes.fyi) by [ossama.is](https://ossama.is).

Edit this file freely to add project-specific conventions. The sections below are a starting point; once you edit them, this file is yours.

To audit a draft against everything below, run `/ai-slop:review` (or `/ai-slop:review-diff` to scope the audit to git-modified lines).

## Language

- **Use American English consistently.** That means analyze (not analyse), behavior (not behaviour), organization (not organisation), modeling (not modelling), color (not colour). Check for British spellings introduced by collaborators or spell-checkers set to the wrong locale.
- **Treat "data" as singular.** "The data shows" and "the data is," not "the data show" or "the data are." Project convention: both forms are accepted in style guides, but we use singular consistently.
- **Use "such as" not "like" to introduce examples.** Write "scenarios such as code completion," not "scenarios like code completion." `Like` is colloquial in this construction; `such as` is the more formal register. Apply this even when the original prose already uses `like` — do not carry it over verbatim into a rewrite. `Like` remains correct as a verb ("readers like terse prose") and in deliberate similes.

## Restricted Words — Use Sparingly

Legitimate words that AI overuses. Each use should be intentional. If a simpler word works, use it.

| Restricted     | Preferred alternative(s)            | When the restricted form is acceptable                                                                                                                                       |
| -------------- | ----------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| utilize        | use                                 | Only when the distinction from "use" matters                                                                                                                                 |
| leverage       | use, apply, employ                  | Only when the lever metaphor is intentional                                                                                                                                  |
| facilitate     | enable, support, help, allow        | n/a                                                                                                                                                                          |
| foster         | encourage, support, promote         | n/a                                                                                                                                                                          |
| streamline     | simplify, reduce, speed up          | Acceptable in process-improvement contexts                                                                                                                                   |
| underscore     | emphasize, highlight, stress        | n/a                                                                                                                                                                          |
| harness        | use, apply, employ                  | n/a                                                                                                                                                                          |
| encompass      | include, cover, span                | n/a                                                                                                                                                                          |
| navigate       | handle, manage, deal with           | Only for literal movement through a UI, website, menu, or file tree (e.g., "navigate the codebook"); never as a metaphor for handling difficulty ("navigate the challenges") |
| landscape      | field, area, environment, situation | n/a                                                                                                                                                                          |
| nuanced        | detailed, subtle, qualified         | n/a                                                                                                                                                                          |
| multifaceted   | complex, varied, many-sided         | n/a                                                                                                                                                                          |
| intricate      | complex, detailed, elaborate        | n/a                                                                                                                                                                          |
| meticulous     | careful, thorough, rigorous         | n/a                                                                                                                                                                          |
| transformative | n/a                                 | Only when genuinely describing transformation                                                                                                                                |

**Standard vocabulary (novel, robust, comprehensive, insights, mitigate, enhance, innovative, paradigm, framework, stakeholder, fundamentally, inherently)** is not restricted. Do not overuse it; if a simpler word works equally well, prefer it.

**Transition words (moreover, furthermore, notably, conversely, crucially, etc.)** are also standard and not restricted. Do not overuse them. If more than two appear in a single paragraph, check whether any can be dropped without losing logical flow.

**Precedence over the trope catalog.** The runtime-fetched trope catalog flags more words than these rules and lists some of the vocabulary above (e.g., robust, paradigm, framework, notably) among its banned words, just as it flags "In summary"/"In conclusion" that the **Formulaic openings and closings** rule permits in a genuine summary position. Where the catalog and a layer rule disagree, the layer rule wins: the catalog supplies candidates to inspect, and these rules state the deliberate exceptions.

## Phrases to Avoid

Stock formulations that read as AI filler or stilted register. Replace each with the plain alternative. The trope catalog (fetched separately) covers the broader banned-phrase list; this section holds project-specific additions.

- **"worked example(s)"** → "example(s)". The qualifier "worked" rarely adds information and reads as padded pedagogical register. Keep it only in the narrow technical sense of a fully solved problem walked through step by step (a textbook "worked solution"), where the contrast with an unsolved exercise is the point.
- **"earn its keep" / "earn its place" / "pull its weight"** → state what the element contributes (e.g., "the opener introduces the list that follows"). The idiom states a plain judgment as figurative filler.

## Terminology Consistency

- **Use one term for one concept.** Once you introduce a term for a concept, use that same term throughout the document. Do not alternate between synonyms for variety; what reads as elegant variation in literary writing creates ambiguity in technical writing. If "code review" is the term, do not switch to "code inspection," "review process," and "code assessment" in subsequent paragraphs.
- **Define terms on first use, then reuse exactly.** If a concept needs a definition or explanation, provide it once. After that, the established term carries the meaning without re-explanation.
- **Synonyms are acceptable only for genuinely different concepts.** If two terms refer to distinct things, use both, but make the distinction explicit.

## Voice

- **Prefer active voice.** Use passive only when the actor is unknown, irrelevant, or when passive genuinely reads better. If a sentence works in active voice, use active voice.
- **Use consistent tense within and across adjacent paragraphs.** Unmotivated tense shifts are distracting. Switch tense only when the temporal frame genuinely changes.

## Punctuation

- **Em-dashes.** Judge each dash on its own: is an em-dash genuinely the right mark, or is it standing in for a period, comma, or parentheses that would read better? Reserve it for a genuine interruption or an appositive that needs setting off; if splitting into two sentences or using a comma works, do that, and never swap an em-dash for parentheses — both signal a sentence doing too much. Count is only a secondary signal: more than 2 to 3 per page-equivalent (~350 words) of running prose flags over-reliance and is worth a second pass, but one dash used wrongly is a worse problem than three used well. Two structural uses are legitimate and are not over-reliance: (a) appositives whose interior already contains commas, where outer commas around the appositive would be ambiguous (`Three reviewers — Alice, Bob, and Carol — flagged the issue`); and (b) a parenthetical that itself contains parentheses, where em dashes stand in for an outer pair of parens to avoid nesting (`the corpus — built from public repositories (GitHub, GitLab) — covers ...`). Em dashes inside quoted source material likewise do not count, since they belong to the quotation, not to the writer.
- **Literal em-dash glyphs in source.** A literal `—` (U+2014) in code-edited source is a tell on its own: editors don't autocorrect `-`/`--` into `—`, so humans type `-`, `--`, or `:` (and `---` in LaTeX). Flag every literal `—` in Markdown, plain text, comments, or `.tex` (outside quoted material and code-span examples, which may show the glyph deliberately, as in the `term — gloss` example below), and replace it with the format's ASCII form. The common case is a uniform `term — gloss` list separator (API references, glossaries): the list is fine, the glyph isn't, so prefer `term: gloss`, a hyphen, or a table. This is about the glyph, not the per-mark judgment in **Em-dashes** above.
- **Colons.** Judge each colon: it is appropriate before a list, a definition, or a deliberate setup-and-payoff that the pause genuinely earns, not as a generic mid-sentence pause. If a colon could be replaced by a period with light rewriting, use the period. Two failure modes to watch for. First, colon-followed-by-list patterns appearing in every other paragraph. Second, colons that have crept in as substitutes for em-dashes or parentheses when those were forbidden. Count is a secondary signal: more than 2 per page-equivalent in running prose flags over-reliance. Headings, table captions, and `figure:`-style labels are exempt; the rule applies to running prose.
- **Introducer punctuation: `:` not `.` before a list or continuation.** When a sentence introduces an enumerated list, a numbered structure (e.g., `(1) ... (2) ... (3) ...`), or a paragraph that grammatically completes or elaborates the introducer, end the introducer with `:`, not `.`. AI text systematically defaults to `.` here. Mechanical test: if the following block is a list or directly continues the introducer, use `:`; if the following block stands as an independent sentence on its own topic, the period is correct. Introducer colons doing this grammatical job are exempt from the colon count above, which targets mid-sentence colons used as filler pauses, em-dash substitutes, or decorative setup.
- **Capitalization after a colon.** In running prose, capitalize the first word after a colon when what follows is a complete sentence (an independent clause). Keep it lowercase when the colon introduces a fragment, phrase, single word, or list. Examples: "We adopt one rule: Capitalize after a colon when a full sentence follows." vs. "We considered three options: speed, accuracy, and cost." Headings and `figure:` / `table:` labels are exempt. Project convention; AI prose reliably defaults to lowercase here regardless of clause completeness. When a colon introduces an enumerated series rather than a single payoff clause, treat it as a list and keep the first word lowercase even if the items are themselves independent clauses; prefer splitting a series of three or more clauses into sentences (see **No list-cramming in a single sentence**), which removes the question.
- **Semicolons.** Judge each semicolon: it is appropriate to join two closely related independent clauses where the connection adds meaning a period would lose, or to separate items in a complex list where commas would create ambiguity. It is not a generic mid-sentence pause or a default substitute for a period when both clauses can stand alone; if it could be replaced by a period with no loss, use the period. Two separate sentences are often more natural. The most common misuse is a semicolon that glues a second independent clause onto the first, often one opening with a pronoun (we, it, this, they, these). Default to a period there. Count is a secondary signal: more than 1 to 2 per page-equivalent in running prose flags over-reliance.
- **Watch the combined load.** Em-dashes, colons, and semicolons all create mid-sentence pauses, and AI text shifts the load between them when any single mark is restricted, so judging each mark alone misses the pattern. The primary test stays per mark: is each pause the right choice? As a combined secondary signal, a page near all three individual ceilings at once (say 3 em-dashes, 2 colons, 2 semicolons) is over-punctuated even though no single ceiling is exceeded; for each mark, ask whether a split into two sentences reads better.
- **Sentence length.** Vary deliberately. Mix short sentences (5 to 10 words) with longer compound ones (25 to 35 words). AI text is detectable by its uniformity (around 15 to 25 words per sentence, low burstiness). Do not homogenize sentence length when editing.
- **Hyphenation of compound modifiers.** AI text over-hyphenates noun-noun stacks placed before another noun ("code-generation benchmarks", "code-translation performance", "prompt-format sensitivity", "data-collection process", "model-evaluation pipeline"). These three-noun stacks are usually unambiguous without the hyphen ("code generation benchmarks"); drop it. Keep the hyphen only when the unhyphenated form invites a real misread, typically when one element is a participle that could re-attach as a verb ("instruction-following ability" stays hyphenated because "instruction following ability" briefly reads as "instruction following" + "ability" with "following" as a verb). Genuine compound adjectives where one element is an adjective or participle (high-quality, well-known, large-scale, fine-grained) keep the hyphen. This rule adjusts the hyphen of a legitimate compound only; an invented compound such as "review-flattening" is a coinage to rewrite, not a hyphen to drop (see **Plain, literal language**).
- **Oxford comma.** Use it, but do not let comma-heavy constructions substitute for clearer sentence structure.

## Structure

- **No formulaic section openings.** Never open a section or subsection with "In today's...", "In the realm of...", "In an era of...", "As we explore...", or "[Topic] has become increasingly...". Start with the substance.
